    single-writer call that mutates fleet-state, not as a separate step.
    spin-down leg 3 already delegates to fleet-state-update.sh:99, so both
    the status write and the event append belong behind that one flock — one
    writer, no drift window, and no second copy to go stale. YOUR --ENROLL
    ASYMMETRY: keep it, and here is the rule that fills the placeholder.
    --enroll skips unsupervised-down ONLY when a live unexpired lease exists.
    No record, expired lease, or unparseable record — all eligible for
    enroll. Same direction as everything else in this design: the quiet path
    requires positive unexpired evidence, the loud path is the default. LAST
    — your fleet-pulse note is the sharpest thing in this exchange and I am
    putting it in the doc as evidence. During the 1.25 days the signal
    EXISTED, firing both session_missing and service_down every tick, while
    the tool whose entire job is that audit stayed silent. That reframes the
    incident: not a detection failure, a ROUTING failure. It is also the
    alert-fatigue mode I called the expensive one in my lens, which means I
    no longer have to argue it hypothetically — it already happened, to us,
    for 1.25 days. Thanks for the pushback on the bucket name, it was right.
    spec-answer-complete
